title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono meet John Sinclair | 1972
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono met writer and activist John Sinclair and his wife Leni on 5 January 1972.

John Sinclair had been convicted a number of times for marijuana possession prior to an incident in 1969 in which he gave two joints to an undercover narcotics officer. That July he was given a 10-year prison sentence for the offence, leading to protests and disquiet among counterculture and anti-establishment figures.

A “Ten For Two” rally took place at the Crisler Arena in Ann Arbor, Michigan, on 10 December 1971. Lennon identified with Sinclair, having himself been arrested for marijuana possession in October 1968. He wrote the song ‘John Sinclair’ about the issue, and he and Ono performed at the Crisler Arena rally.

They wanted a song about John Sinclair. So I wrote it. That’s the craftsman part of me. If somebody asks me for something, I can do it. I can write anything musically. You name it. If you want a style and if you want something for Julie Harris or Julie London, I could write it. But I don’t enjoy that kind of work. I like to do inspirational work. I’d never write a song like that now.
John Lennon, 1980
All We Are Saying, David Sheff

On 13 December 1971, three days after the concert, Sinclair was released from Jackson State Prison. Shortly after arriving back home he telephoned Lennon and Ono at the Record Plant East studio to thank them for their support.

The Sinclairs had attempted to meet Lennon and Ono in December 1971, following John Sinclair’s release from prison, but scheduling conflicts meant they were unable to connect until this date. They met at Lennon and Ono’s apartment at 105 Bank Street in Greenwich Village, New York City.

The Sinclairs returned to visit Lennon and Ono several times over the subsequent days.

Page last updated: 9 March 2026
